notes: Identity assessment: supplied cache is a Scribd-hosted transcription of the primary article, with web navigation surrounding the article. The article header gives Norm Theory: Comparing Reality to Its Alternatives, Daniel Kahneman and Dale T. Miller, Psychological Review, 1986, Vol. 93, No. 2, 136-153, matching the neutral original reference. Article text runs from the abstract and p. 136 through references and receipt/revision dates at the end, rather than only an abstract/excerpt. The supplied DOI is not printed in the inspected header, so DOI identity is not independently established by a DOI string. No PDF was supplied; layout/OCR could not be checked against a rendered PDF. Target correspondence unresolved: study_o=1 and locator p.10, with an empty description, do not uniquely identify an unnumbered demonstration/outcome on printed p.145. Candidates: routine versus exceptional driving route (Adams/White), upset judgments, 18%/82%, N=92; rare versus frequent hitchhiker pickup (Jones/Smith), regret judgments 88%/12% and criticism judgments 23%/77%, shared scenario N=138; delayed versus on-time missed flights (C/D), upset judgments 96%/4%, N=138; stock switching versus retaining (Paul/George), regret judgments 8%/92%, N=138. These printed N values are candidate respondent counts attached to demonstrations, not an established analytic N for either assigned row. Exclusions are not documented in these passages. Page 145 supplies response percentages and narrative conclusions, with no printed inferential test statistic or p value attached to these demonstrations. Do not convert percentages to a test statistic or calculate p. The flight and stock examples explicitly cite Kahneman & Tversky (1982); the present source alone cannot replace that separate primary work if either is ultimately the intended target. Neither audit row is assigned to a candidate by order or numeric agreement. No N arithmetic was performed. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
